title: Connected agents vs A2A tool
summary: The classic Connected Agents tool is not available in the new Foundry Agent Service. Use the A2A tool for peer agents, Agent Framework orchestration inside hosted code, or Workflows (preview, retiring 2026-12-01).
useIf: One Foundry agent must delegate to another agent, in or outside Foundry, and you are migrating off Connected Agents.
avoidIf: The peer is a plain function or API: use a tool. Use A2A only when the peer is a real agent with its own reasoning.

explain.md: The Connected Agents tool from the classic Agents API is **not available** in the new Foundry Agent Service. The docs name two replacements: the **A2A tool**, which connects to any A2A-compatible endpoint including another Foundry agent exposed as an A2A endpoint, and **Workflows**, which orchestrate Foundry agents declaratively [[r21]]. Workflows are preview and retire on 2026-12-01, and classic agents retire on 2027-03-31 [[r11]]. For new multi-agent work in code, the GA page points to Microsoft Agent Framework (see the Agent Framework chapter) [[r9]].

The A2A tool has two tool types. `a2a` targets A2A protocol 1.0 and is **GA**. `a2a_preview` targets 0.3 and stays **preview** for existing integrations [[r21]]. When your agent calls a remote agent through the tool, the remote agent processes the request and your agent uses the response, then keeps managing the conversation [[r21]]. A2A v1.0.0 was released on 2026-03-12, with breaking changes from 0.3 such as renamed operations [[tr7]]. Store credentials in a project connection and consider adding the tool through a toolbox [[r21]]. Creating the A2A project connection needs Foundry Project Manager, and testing needs Foundry User [[r21]].

explain.title: A2A tool call path
explain.alt: A user asks a Foundry agent. The agent calls a remote A2A agent through the a2a tool. The remote agent responds and the Foundry agent answers the user and keeps the conversation.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant F as Foundry agent
  participant R as Remote A2A agent
  U->>F: Question
  F->>R: Request through the a2a tool
  R-->>F: Response
  F-->>U: Answer, conversation stays with F

explain.caption: Calling a Foundry agent as an A2A endpoint: limits on 2026-10-13
head: Aspect
Documented behavior
rows: A2A v1.0 over JSON-RPC only. With no version selector Foundry serves 0.3, so send `A2A-Version: 1.0`
The agent must use the Responses protocol
Entra only, caller needs the Foundry Agent Consumer role or higher
Tasks and contexts are kept 60 days from last write

explain.title: Agent card path
explain.md: For agents registered in Foundry Control Plane the default agent card path is `/.well-known/agent-card.json` [[r23]].

use: The peer is a separately owned agent that you cannot or should not embed
You want a standard protocol rather than a Foundry-only mechanism
You need the peer to keep its own state and reasoning
avoid: All agents live in one codebase and one team: orchestrate in-process with Agent Framework instead of network hops
New designs built on Workflows, which are preview and retire on 2026-12-01
The peer is a stateless function: expose it as an OpenAPI or MCP tool

Preview is not allowed: use `a2a` (GA, v1.0) and avoid `a2a_preview`
The pattern must be declarative and short-lived: Workflows work today but plan the retirement

pitfalls.symptom: Remote Foundry agent answers in an older protocol shape
pitfalls.cause: With no version selector Foundry serves A2A 0.3

pitfalls.symptom: Caller gets 403 on a Foundry A2A endpoint
pitfalls.cause: The calling identity lacks the Foundry Agent Consumer role on the target project
pitfalls.fix: Grant Foundry Agent Consumer or higher and use Entra auth [[r21]].

pitfalls.symptom: A new design depends on Workflows and the team plans a rewrite
pitfalls.fix: Pick Agent Framework code orchestration or A2A for new work [[r11]].

scenarios.title: A peer team owns the specialist agent
scenarios.situation: A Foundry agent needs a tax-rules specialist that another team runs in its own container and exposes over A2A. The specialist's internals are private.
unknowns: Which A2A version does the peer serve?
How does the peer authenticate callers?
scenarios.question: How do you connect them?

options.name: A2A tool with the `a2a` (GA, v1.0) type and a project connection
options.why: Standard protocol, credentials in a connection, peer stays opaque.
options.tradeoff: You depend on the peer's version support and uptime.

options.name: Wrap the peer as an MCP tool
options.why: Easy to consume as a tool.
options.tradeoff: You lose A2A task semantics and an opaque agent looks like a function.

options.name: Copy the specialist's logic into your agent
options.tradeoff: Right only when the peer is retired and you inherit it.

flips.if: The peer is a plain REST API

scenarios.title: Three agents, one team, one release
scenarios.situation: One team owns three Foundry agents that run in a fixed order with shared state and a single release train. They used Connected Agents in the classic service.
unknowns: Do any steps need to run in parallel?
scenarios.question: What replaces Connected Agents?

options.name: Agent Framework orchestration inside one hosted agent
options.why: Code-defined control flow, no network hops, no retiring dependency.
options.tradeoff: You write and test the orchestration, and the hosted GA label is unconfirmed.

options.name: A2A tool between the three agents
options.tradeoff: Extra hops, auth and version handling for agents the team already owns.

options.name: Foundry Workflows (preview)
options.why: Retires on 2026-12-01 and the design must outlive it.
options.tradeoff: Fine for short-lived experiments before the retirement.

flips.if: The agents will be split among teams
The flow is a short pilot
flips.then: Workflows are acceptable until the retirement.

scenarios.takeaway: Do not build long-lived designs on a preview feature with a retirement date.

quiz.q: Which tool type targets A2A protocol 1.0 and is GA in Foundry?
quiz.explain: `a2a` is GA and targets 1.0. `a2a_preview` targets 0.3 and is preview. Connected Agents is not in the new service.

quiz.q: Which are documented limits of calling a Foundry agent as an A2A endpoint?
quiz.explain: The incoming A2A endpoint is v1.0 over JSON-RPC only, text only, without streaming, and needs the Responses protocol. gRPC and HTTP+JSON are not offered.

quiz.q: A design must stay in service for years. Which option is a poor base because of a published retirement date?
options: Agent Framework orchestration in hosted code
Direct tool calls to an OpenAPI service
quiz.explain: Workflows (preview) retire on 2026-12-01. The other options have no announced retirement in the sources checked on 2026-10-13.

flashcards.front: What replaces Connected Agents in the new Foundry Agent Service?
flashcards.back: The A2A tool (any A2A endpoint, including a Foundry agent exposed as one), Foundry Workflows (preview, retire 2026-12-01), or Agent Framework orchestration in your own code.

flashcards.front: Which header makes a Foundry agent serve A2A 1.0?
flashcards.back: `A2A-Version: 1.0`. With no version selector Foundry serves 0.3.
